subject: Materials Science
title: Designing with Defects
description: A fast breakdown of Designing with Defects for builders.

hook.text: A perfect crystal would be useless — too brittle, no conductivity control, impossible to shape.

buildup.text: Materials engineers don't eliminate defects — they choose which types to introduce and control.

discovery.text: Strengthening combines solid solution, precipitation, work hardening, and grain refinement — all defect-based.

twist.text: Superalloys for jet turbines use all four mechanisms simultaneously — maximizing every defect interaction.

climax.text: Single-crystal turbine blades eliminate grain boundaries entirely — perfection where it matters most.

punchline.text: Master the defects and you master the material — imperfection is the best tool.

quiz.question: Why are single-crystal turbine blades used in jet engines?
options: Eliminating grain boundaries prevents creep failure at high temperatures
They are lighter than polycrystalline blades
